metadata.title: Online Retail Marketplace Residuality Stress Test
metadata.description: Explore how the retail marketplace would need to change when software agents buy for people, product law changes, fulfillment routes close, goods are recalled, creator-led demand spikes, or a competitor changes price expectations.
metadata.naiveArchitecture: A shopper searches a catalog, opens a product page, selects one seller offer, checks out, and receives an order from the chosen fulfillment path. Returns and refunds operate after delivery.
metadata.residualArchitecture: Instead of binding the product page, seller offer, inventory, delivery path, buyer, and order into one happy-path checkout, the adapted design manages and versions each of them separately. Human shoppers and software agents use the same clear offer contract. Inventory and delivery can be replanned, and unsafe goods can be quarantined, without losing the customer's order or the evidence behind each decision.
metadata.note: The rows deliberately mix customer, regulatory, physical, supply-chain, channel, and competitive context. No row is ranked by chance or filtered as an edge case.

source.title: Residues: Time, Change, and Uncertainty in Software Architecture
source.author: Barry M. O'Reilly

stressors.name: Personal AI agents become the primary buyers instead of people browsing pages
stressors.detection: Authenticated agent traffic, structured-offer API demand, delegated-purchase attempts, customer research, and declining page-led conversion share.
stressors.attractor: Discovery, comparison, and purchase happen through delegated machine intent; page placement and persuasive UI lose leverage while offer semantics, authority, constraints, and post-purchase explanation become decisive.
stressors.businessReaction: Let customers delegate bounded purchasing authority, expose comparable offers and delivery promises to agents, preserve consent and fraud controls, and explain every commitment to the account holder.
stressors.residue: Create a channel-independent offer and purchase-intent contract. Buyer, beneficiary, payer, delegate, budget, substitution policy, evidence, and expiry are explicit; human pages and agent APIs are adapters over the same catalog, pricing, promise, and order decisions.

impacts.effect: Being the trusted default extends from the website to customer-controlled buying agents.
The shopper can delegate shortlisting and purchase while retaining constraints and an understandable decision record.
Turns intent into structured constraints and ranked offer evidence usable by either a person or an agent.
Search-to-detail is no longer sufficient; discovery efficiency must include agent shortlist-to-approved-purchase flow.
Adds delegation, review, explanation, and intervention surfaces around machine-generated shopping intent.
Publishes signed, versioned offer and purchase-intent contracts for customer-authorized agents.
Models the account holder, delegate, payer, beneficiary, scopes, budgets, and revocation separately.
Returns evidence-bearing recommendations under declared constraints rather than opaque page personalization.
Owns discovery quality across human and delegated-machine channels.
Moves competitive comparison toward who supplies the most trusted machine-readable commerce decision layer.
Carries shopper intent, delegation, comparable offers, authorization, explanation, and purchase across human and agent channels.

stressors.name: A regulator requires product provenance to be proven before an offer can be displayed
stressors.detection: Regulatory text, marketplace notices, customs enforcement, seller document gaps, audit requests, and blocked-offer events.
stressors.attractor: A commercially valid listing is not necessarily a legally eligible offer; eligibility varies by jurisdiction, seller, item origin, evidence version, customer type, and time.
stressors.businessReaction: Collect evidence once, decide offer eligibility at every relevant boundary, suppress or remediate non-compliant offers, and produce an auditable explanation to sellers and regulators.
stressors.residue: Separate product content from an evidence-bearing seller offer. A policy decision service evaluates seller, product, provenance, jurisdiction, channel, and effective-time facts; browse, ads, checkout, and fulfillment consume the same signed eligibility result.

impacts.effect: Marketplace trust becomes preventive eligibility backed by reusable evidence, not post-listing enforcement.
Keeping non-compliant offers off the marketplace starts before an offer reaches any channel.
Each decision retains the evidence set, policy version, effective time, and explanation used.
Verification completeness must be measurable per active offer and jurisdiction, not only per seller account.
Needs evidence lifecycle, policy simulation, remediation, appeal, and regulator-ready decision views.
Maintains seller identity and evidence without embedding every market's eligibility rules.
Links origin and authenticity claims to evidence and affected offers.
Produces a versioned, explainable eligibility decision reusable across all commerce surfaces.
Owns the cross-channel policy contract and evidence standard.
Makes provable offer eligibility and seller remediation speed a marketplace differentiator.
Applies the same evidence and eligibility decision before browse, advertising, checkout, and fulfillment exposure.

stressors.name: Flooding makes a major fulfillment region inaccessible for several weeks
stressors.detection: Carrier embargoes, weather and civil-protection feeds, facility state, route failures, inventory scans, and delivery-promise exception telemetry.
stressors.attractor: Sellable inventory still exists in systems, but the planned nodes and routes cannot fulfill promises; demand shifts to neighboring regions and static inventory ownership turns into widespread customer disappointment.
stressors.businessReaction: Stop making impossible promises, re-plan from alternative nodes or sellers, reserve scarce capacity, offer substitutions, and proactively resolve orders that no longer have a credible path.
stressors.residue: Treat a delivery promise as a versioned fulfillment plan over fungible supply, capacity, route, and service constraints. The order owns the customer commitment; eligible inventory and route bindings can change until controlled execution boundaries.

impacts.effect: Post-purchase reliability depends on detecting and re-planning physical network states before customers feel them.
Keeping promises honest includes withdrawing and replacing a plan that has become physically impossible.
Chooses an alternate node, seller, route, service level, or substitution from the remaining feasible options.
At-risk promise lead time begins when physical capacity becomes invalid, before the carrier misses a scan.
Shows a revised credible plan and customer choices rather than repeatedly delaying the original one.
Exposes inventory with location, accessibility, reservation, and substitution semantics.
Computes promises from current capacity and keeps alternate fulfillment plans available.
Separates the customer commitment from replaceable fulfillment bindings and records every re-plan.
Owns cross-node promise preservation and the constrained-network operating mode.
Replans inventory, capacity, route, service, and customer choices around the surviving network.
Makes region-scale fulfillment continuity and proactive promise recovery a retail-logistics benchmark.

stressors.name: A manufacturer recalls one production lot mixed across first- and third-party inventory
stressors.detection: Manufacturer notices, regulator alerts, lot and serial evidence, customer reports, seller disclosures, and returns inspection.
stressors.attractor: Product-page identity is too coarse: only some physical units are unsafe, they have moved through several owners and fulfillment modes, and affected customers need action before they initiate a return.
stressors.businessReaction: Identify every affected unit and order, quarantine remaining stock, stop new offers, notify customers, provide replacement or refund, and prove the response to authorities.
stressors.residue: Maintain a trace graph from evidence and production lot through seller offer, physical unit or batch, inventory movement, shipment, order, and beneficiary. Safety actions target graph sets and propagate idempotently across channels and fulfillment owners.

impacts.effect: Trust includes proactive protection after purchase when a precise subset of units becomes unsafe.
Problem resolution can begin from marketplace evidence before the shopper notices the problem.
Presents a verified recall, the affected order, safe disposal, and replacement or refund in one flow.
Regulator response time includes trace completeness and customer remediation coverage.
Needs recall scope, quarantine progress, customer reach, remediation, and audit views.
Links catalog identity to lot-level evidence without treating one product page as one physical product.
Quarantines affected stock and preserves chain-of-custody evidence through movement and disposal.
Executes proactive replacement, refund, and safe-disposal paths independent of a normal return request.
Coordinates the evidence standard and decision boundary for cross-owner product safety actions.
Propagates lot-level recall scope through offers, stock, orders, customers, quarantine, and redress.
Makes first- and third-party lot traceability and proactive remediation a marketplace safety benchmark.

stressors.name: A creator livestream makes an unfamiliar seller's product the day's largest order burst
stressors.detection: Referral and creator traffic, agent and API intent, offer-view acceleration, cart reservations, seller inventory updates, and promise-capacity saturation.
stressors.attractor: Demand forms outside normal search and forecasting loops; trust, inventory, and delivery capacity must be decided in seconds for an offer with little sales history.
stressors.businessReaction: Admit only eligible offers, expose honest available quantity and promises, meter reservations, re-plan fulfillment, and give buyers consistent substitution or wait choices across every channel.
stressors.residue: No new structural change is required: channel-independent purchase intent, evidence-based offer eligibility, and replaceable fulfillment plans already let creator traffic use the same governed offer, capacity, and order contracts.

impacts.effect: A seller can capture sudden demand without bypassing readiness, eligibility, inventory, or promise controls.
Buyability remains a governed offer state while traffic source and volume change.
Priority-ASIN conversion can be interpreted with eligibility, reservation, and promise-capacity context.
Shows sellers how eligibility, quantity, capacity, and promise constraints govern the burst.
Accepts creator and agent channels through the existing signed intent and offer contract.
Meters reservations against usable, location-aware inventory rather than unqualified seller quantity.
Can enable creator-led demand as a channel configuration without a separate marketplace core.
Absorbs livestream commerce mechanics while preserving the marketplace's trust and fulfillment advantages.
Seller growth can absorb creator-led demand without bypassing trust, inventory, and delivery promises.
Keeps the unfamiliar seller's offer eligible, buyable, capacity-aware, and explainable through the burst.

stressors.name: A competitor subsidizes factory-direct prices below local seller economics
stressors.detection: Competitive baskets, seller churn interviews, price-index movement, cross-border delivery complaints, and category-level conversion loss.
stressors.attractor: Shoppers anchor on a lower item price while local sellers cannot match it; marketplace differentiation shifts to trust, delivery certainty, returns, membership value, and total landed cost.
stressors.businessReaction: Make total value and service levels explicit, let sellers choose differentiated fulfillment and trust propositions, and invest selectively where speed, certainty, authenticity, or resolution change customer choice.
stressors.residue: Represent an offer as a bundle of item price, landed cost, delivery commitment, provenance, seller terms, service entitlement, and resolution promise. Ranking and experimentation optimize declared customer outcomes rather than hiding every distinction inside one price score.

impacts.effect: Seller growth depends on controllable service differentiation when pure price competition is structurally unattractive.
Choosing the right product includes comparing landed cost, confidence, delivery, and recourse rather than item price alone.
Makes material service and trust differences comparable at the decision point.
Service economics must connect promise tiers and resolution cost to retained demand.
Explains why offers differ beyond price and lets customers choose the service bundle they value.
Publishes total landed cost and offer-health context without erasing non-price attributes.
Presents fulfillment, provenance, entitlement, and resolution commitments as first-class offer terms.
Owns outcome-based offer comparison and tests where service differentiation defeats a price gap.
Frames the competitive response around a different value architecture rather than automatic price matching.
Compares total landed cost, delivery, provenance, entitlement, and recovery as one understandable customer choice.
